questions.question: In what proportion must a grocer mix rice at Rs. 32/kg and Rs. 39/kg so that on selling the mixture at Rs. 43.2/kg there is a profit of 20%.
questions.questionHtml: In what proportion must a grocer mix rice at Rs. 32/kg and Rs. 39/kg so that on selling the mixture at Rs. 43.2/kg there is a profit of 20%.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

CP of Mixture = SP ÷ (1 + Profit%)

CPmix = 43.2 ÷ 1.2 = ₹36/kg

By Alligation: (39 − 36) : (36 − 32)

Ratio = 3 : 4

∴ The correct answer is 3 ∶ 4.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price of first variety (CP1) = ₹32/kg

Cost Price of second variety (CP2) = ₹39/kg

Selling Price of mixture (SPmix) = ₹43.2/kg

Profit percentage = 20%

Formula Used:

CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 + Profit%]

Calculations:

⇒ CP of the mixture = (43.2 × 100) ÷ (100 + 20)

⇒ CP of the mixture = 4320 ÷ 120 = ₹36/kg

⇒ Using the Rule of Alligation:

⇒ Quantity of Rice 1 : Quantity of Rice 2 = (CP2 − CPmix) : (CPmix − CP1)

⇒ Ratio = (39 − 36) : (36 − 32)

⇒ Ratio = 3 : 4

∴ The correct answer is 3 ∶ 4.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

It is used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a specified price. Ratio = (Dearer Price − Mean Price) : (Mean Price − Cheaper Price).

Consistency of Units

While applying alligation, all values (CP1, CP2, and Mean Price) must be in the same unit. If SP is given, it must be converted to CP first.

Profit and Loss Relation

Cost Price = [Selling Price ÷ (100 + Profit%)] × 100 or CP = SP ÷ Multiplying Factor.

questions.question: 2/3 of a milk-water mixture was milk. There was 21 litres of the mixture. If 4 litres of water is added to it, Then find the percentage of milk in the new mixture.
questions.questionHtml: 2/3 of a milk-water mixture was milk. There was 21 litres of the mixture. If 4 litres of water is added to it, Then find the percentage of milk in the new mixture.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial Milk = 2/3 × 21 = 14 litres.

New Total Mixture = 21 + 4 = 25 litres.

New Milk Percentage = (14 / 25) × 100 = 56%.

∴ The correct answer is 56.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial volume of mixture = 21 litres

Portion of milk = 2/3

Volume of water added = 4 litres

Calculations:

⇒ Quantity of Milk = 2/3 × 21 = 14 litres

⇒ Quantity of Water = 21 − 14 = 7 litres

⇒ New quantity of Water = 7 + 4 = 11 litres

⇒ Total quantity of New Mixture = 14 (Milk) + 11 (Water) = 25 litres

⇒ Percentage of Milk in new mixture = (Milk / Total Mixture) × 100

⇒ Percentage of Milk = (14 / 25) × 100

⇒ Percentage of Milk = 14 × 4 = 56%

∴ The correct answer is 56.

Additional Information

Concentration Formula

The concentration of a component is given by: (Volume of Component / Total Volume of Mixture) × 100.

Mixture Addition Rule

When only one component is added, the quantity of the other component remains constant, while the total volume increases.

Ratio and Proportion

If milk and water are in ratio a:b, then Milk % = [a / (a + b)] × 100.

questions.question: 80 liters of a mixture of alcohol and water contains 60% alcohol. If 'X' liters of water is added to this mixture, then the percentage of alcohol in the new mixture becomes 40%. What is the value of 'X'?
questions.questionHtml: 80 liters of a mixture of alcohol and water contains 60% alcohol. If 'X' liters of water is added to this mixture, then the percentage of alcohol in the new mixture becomes 40%. What is the value of 'X'?
questions.solution:
Amount of alcohol in 80 litre of mixture = 60% of 80 = 48 litres

Amount of water in 80 litre of mixture =80 - 48 = 32 litres

32 + X = 60/100 × (80 + X) ⇒ 5(32 + X) = 3(80 + X) ⇒ 160 + 5X = 240 + 3X ⇒ X = 40

questions.question: A mixture of milk and water contains 18 parts of milk and 8 parts of water. How much fraction of the mixture should be removed and replaced by water so the ratio of water and milk are equal?
questions.questionHtml: A mixture of milk and water contains 18 parts of milk and 8 parts of water. How much fraction of the mixture should be removed and replaced by water so the ratio of water and milk are equal?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial parts of Milk = 18 and Water = 8. Total = 26 units.

To make the ratio equal, each component must be 26 ÷ 2 = 13 units.

Reduction needed in Milk = 18 − 13 = 5 units.

Fraction of mixture to be replaced = (Quantity of Milk to be removed) ÷ (Initial quantity of Milk).

Fraction = 5/18.

∴ The correct answer is 5/18.

Alternate Method

Given: Initial Milk = 18 parts, Initial Water = 8 parts.

Calculations:

⇒ Total initial mixture = 18 + 8 = 26 units.

⇒ Let the fraction of mixture removed and replaced by water be k.

⇒ Quantity of Milk in the remaining mixture = 18 − (18 × k).

⇒ For equal ratio, Milk must be half of the total volume.

⇒ Final Milk = 26 ÷ 2 = 13 units.

⇒ 18 − 18k = 13

⇒ 18k = 18 − 13

⇒ 18k = 5

⇒ k = 5/18

∴ The correct answer is 5/18.

Additional Information

Mixture Replacement Rule

When a part of a mixture is replaced by one of its ingredients, the total volume remains constant, but the concentration of the replaced ingredient increases.

Final Concentration Formula

Final amount of liquid = Initial amount × (1 − Quantity Replaced ÷ Total Quantity). This is used repeatedly for multiple replacements.

Ratio Balance Method

If Milk:Water = a:b is changed to 1:1 by replacing with water, the fraction removed is (a − b) ÷ (2a).

questions.question: The initial ratio of sugar to flour in dough was 2 : 7. To 9 kg of the dough, John added more sugar to make the sugar to flour ratio 2 : 5. How much sugar did Johan later add?
questions.questionHtml: The initial ratio of sugar to flour in dough was 2 : 7. To 9 kg of the dough, John added more sugar to make the sugar to flour ratio 2 : 5. How much sugar did Johan later add?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial Ratio (Sugar:Flour) = 2 : 7 ⇒ Total 9 units = 9 kg ⇒ 1 unit = 1 kg.

Initial Sugar = 2 kg and Initial Flour = 7 kg.

New Ratio = 2 : 5. Since only Sugar is added, Flour remains 7 kg.

⇒ 5 units = 7 kg ⇒ 1 unit = 1.4 kg.

New Sugar = 2 × 1.4 = 2.8 kg.

Sugar added = 2.8 − 2 = 0.8 kg = 800 g.

∴ The correct answer is 800 g.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Weight of dough = 9 kg

Initial Ratio of Sugar to Flour = 2 : 7

New Ratio of Sugar to Flour = 2 : 5

Formula Used:

Component Quantity = Total Weight × (Component Ratio Part ÷ Total Ratio Parts)

Calculations:

⇒ Initial Sugar = (2 ÷ (2 + 7)) × 9 = (2 ÷ 9) × 9 = 2 kg

⇒ Initial Flour = (7 ÷ 9) × 9 = 7 kg

⇒ Let the amount of Sugar added be x kg.

⇒ New Sugar = (2 + x) kg

⇒ New Ratio = (2 + x) ÷ 7 = 2 ÷ 5

⇒ 5 × (2 + x) = 2 × 7

⇒ 10 + 5x = 14

⇒ 5x = 4

⇒ x = 4 ÷ 5 = 0.8 kg

⇒ 0.8 kg = 0.8 × 1000 g = 800 g

∴ The correct answer is 800 g.

Additional Information

Constant Quantity Concept

In mixture problems, identify the component whose quantity does not change and use it as a reference to find the new total weight.

Ratio Balancing

To balance ratios when one part is constant, multiply the ratios by suitable numbers so that the constant part has the same number of units in both ratios.

Unit Conversion

Always ensure consistency in units. Multiply kilograms by 1000 to convert to grams (1 kg = 1000 g).

questions.question: A container contains two liquids, X and Y, in the ratio 5 ∶ 3. When 8 liters of the mixture is drawn off, and the container is filled with liquid Y, the ratio of X to Y becomes 2 ∶ 3. How many liters of liquid X was in the container initially?
questions.questionHtml: A container contains two liquids, X and Y, in the ratio 5 ∶ 3. When 8 liters of the mixture is drawn off, and the container is filled with liquid Y, the ratio of X to Y becomes 2 ∶ 3. How many liters of liquid X was in the container initially?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since only liquid Y is added, the quantity of liquid X only changes when the mixture is drawn out.

Initial fraction of X = 5/8, and Final fraction of X = 2/5.

Using replacement logic: Final fraction = Initial fraction × [1 − (Replaced quantity ÷ Total Volume V)].

⇒ 2/5 = 5/8 × (1 − 8/V) ⇒ 16/25 = 1 − 8/V ⇒ 8/V = 9/25 ⇒ V = 200/9 liters.

Initial quantity of X in the container = 5/8 × 200/9 = 125/9 = 13 8/9 liters.

∴ The correct answer is 13 8/9 liters.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Initial ratio of X to Y = 5 : 3.

⇒ Mixture drawn out = 8 liters.

⇒ Pure liquid Y added = 8 liters.

⇒ Final ratio of X to Y = 2 : 3.

Formula Used:

⇒ By the Rule of Alligation, comparing the concentration (fraction) of liquid X in the mixture components.

Calculations:

⇒ Fraction of X in the initial mixture = 5 / (5 + 3) = 5/8.

⇒ Fraction of X in the added pure liquid Y = 0.

⇒ Fraction of X in the final mixture = 2 / (2 + 3) = 2/5.

⇒ Ratio of (Initial mixture remaining) : (Added pure liquid Y) = (2/5 − 0) : (5/8 − 2/5).

⇒ Ratio = 2/5 : (25/40 − 16/40) = 2/5 : 9/40 = 16/40 : 9/40 = 16 : 9.

⇒ The added liquid Y corresponds to 9 ratio parts, which is given as 8 liters.

⇒ Total capacity of the mixture = 16 parts + 9 parts = 25 parts.

⇒ Since 9 parts = 8 liters, Total mixture capacity = 25 × (8 / 9) = 200/9 liters.

⇒ Initial quantity of liquid X = (5 / 8) × Total mixture.

⇒ Initial quantity of liquid X = 5/8 × 200/9 = 125/9 = 13 8/9 liters.

∴ The correct answer is 13 8/9 liters.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

It establishes the ratio in which two components of different concentrations are mixed. Ratio = (C2 − Cm) : (Cm − C1), where Cm is the final mixture concentration.

Replacement Formula in Mixtures

When 'y' quantity is drawn from a mixture and replaced with a pure ingredient repeatedly for 'n' times, the quantity of the original ingredient remaining is: Initial Quantity × [1 − (y ÷ Total Volume)]n.

Maintaining Total Volume

In replacement problems where the drawn quantity equals the added pure liquid, the total volume of the mixture remains constant throughout the entire process.

questions.question: The ratio of alcohol to water in three types of drugs of equal quantity is 2 ∶ 5, 5 ∶ 9, and 8 ∶ 13 respectively. An equal quantity of all three drugs is mixed. Find the ratio of alcohol to water after mixing
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of alcohol to water in three types of drugs of equal quantity is 2 ∶ 5, 5 ∶ 9, and 8 ∶ 13 respectively. An equal quantity of all three drugs is mixed. Find the ratio of alcohol to water after mixing
questions.solution:
Alcohol in first drug = 2 ÷ (2 + 5) = 2/7, Water in first drug = 5/7

Alcohol in second drug = 5 ÷ (5 + 9) = 5/14, Water in second drug = 9/14

Alcohol in third drug = 8 ÷ (8 + 13) = 8/21, Water in third drug = 13/21

Total alcohol = (2/7) + (5/14) + (8/21) = 43/42

Total water = (5/7) + (9/14) + (13/21) = 83/42

Ratio of alcohol to water = 43 ∶ 83

questions.question: A mixture of acid and water contains 20 percent acid. When 10 litres of water is added to the mixture, then the percentage of acid becomes 15 percent. What is the original quantity of mixture ?
questions.questionHtml: A mixture of acid and water contains 20 percent acid. When 10 litres of water is added to the mixture, then the percentage of acid becomes 15 percent. What is the original quantity of mixture ?
questions.solution:
Acid : Water = 1 : 4, Let ratio be x, 4x

x/(4x + 10) = 15/85 ⇒ x/(4x + 10) = 3/17 ⇒ 17x = 3(4x + 10) ⇒ 17x = 12x + 30 ⇒ x = 6 litres

x = 6, then 4x = 24, Total = 6 + 24 = 30 litres

questions.question: A milkman buys milk at Rs 20 per liter. He mixes 4 L of water in a 10-liter container full of pure milk. Find the gain% observed by the milkman, if the milkman swears to sell the mixture at his cost price.
questions.questionHtml: A milkman buys milk at Rs 20 per liter. He mixes 4 L of water in a 10-liter container full of pure milk. Find the gain% observed by the milkman, if the milkman swears to sell the mixture at his cost price.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When water is added to milk and the mixture is sold at the Cost Price (CP) of pure milk, the Gain% is simply the ratio of water to milk.

Gain % = (Quantity of Water / Quantity of Milk) × 100

Given: Water = 4 L, Milk = 10 L

Gain % = (4 / 10) × 100 = 40%

∴ The correct answer is 40%.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Cost Price (CP) of milk = ₹20 per liter

⇒ Quantity of pure milk = 10 L

⇒ Quantity of water added = 4 L

Formula Used:

⇒ Total CP = Quantity × Rate

⇒ Gain % = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) = 10 L × ₹20/L = ₹200

⇒ Total Quantity of mixture = 10 L + 4 L = 14 L

⇒ Selling Price (SP) of mixture = 14 L × ₹20/L = ₹280

⇒ Total Gain = SP − CP = ₹280 − ₹200 = ₹80

⇒ Gain % = (80 / 200) × 100

⇒ Gain % = 40%

∴ The correct answer is 40%.

Additional Information

Profit in Adulteration

When a seller mixes an impurity (costing zero) and sells the mixture at the cost price of the original item, the Profit % = (Quantity of Impurity / Quantity of Original Item) × 100.

Weighted Average Principle

The price of the mixture is the weighted average of the prices of individual components: (n1c1 + n2c2) / (n1 + n2), where water price c2 is usually zero.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

Profit % can also be calculated as [Error / (True Value − Error)] × 100 when weight manipulation is involved instead of physical mixing.

questions.question: Solutions A and B contain acid and water in the ratio 4 ∶ 3 and 9 ∶ 5, respectively. Four litres of solution A is mixed with 5 litres of solution B. What is the ratio of acid and water in the resulting mixture?
questions.questionHtml: Solutions A and B contain acid and water in the ratio 4 ∶ 3 and 9 ∶ 5, respectively. Four litres of solution A is mixed with 5 litres of solution B. What is the ratio of acid and water in the resulting mixture?
questions.solution:
Total acid after mixing of two solution = 4(4/7) + 5(9/14)

⇒ 16/7 + 45/14 = 77/14 = 11/2

Total water after mixing of two solution = 4(3/7) + 5(5/14)

⇒ 12/7 + 25/14 = 49/14 = 7/2 ⇒ Ratio = 11/2 : 7/2 = 11 : 7

questions.question: A milkman has a mixture of milk in which the ratio of milk and water is 7 : 4. He sold 55 litres of this mixture and added 20 litres of pure water to the mixture. Now the ratio of milk and water in the mixture becomes 7 : 6. Find the new quantity of this mixture.
questions.questionHtml: A milkman has a mixture of milk in which the ratio of milk and water is 7 : 4. He sold 55 litres of this mixture and added 20 litres of pure water to the mixture. Now the ratio of milk and water in the mixture becomes 7 : 6. Find the new quantity of this mixture.
questions.solution:
Let milk and water be 7x and 4x respectively,

7x + 4x = 55 ⟹ 11x = 55 ⟹ x = 5

35 L Milk, 20 L Water removed,

After adding 20 L water

7x / (4x + 20) = 7 / 6 ⟹ 6x = 4x + 20 ⟹ x = 10

New quantity = 70 + 60 = 130 L.
